title: A rapid acquisition pathway can still produce slow delivery when the technology is not mature
source_unit: GAO-26-108457 annual assessment of 104 of DOD's costliest weapon programs and selected rapid-acquisition efforts
geography: United States Department of Defense weapon-system acquisition programs; major defense acquisition and Middle Tier of Acquisition portfolios

observations.period: 2026 annual assessment; program status through the report's review period

denominator.unit: DOD weapon programs selected by cost and acquisition status

average_delivery_time.unit: average time frame to deliver a capability across reviewed major programs

middle_tier_portfolio.value: at least 49 billion planned across 23 of the most expensive Middle Tier of Acquisition programs
middle_tier_portfolio.unit: planned acquisition dollars and program count

immature_entry.value: 18 of 40 programs entered the Middle Tier pathway with immature technologies

fieldable_capability.value: some Middle Tier programs ended without delivering a fieldable capability; technologies in 7 of 8 reviewed programs remained immature and required additional development

battlefield_effect.unit: missing operational use, reliability, sustainment, warfighter effect, and adversary response

observations.method: GAO assessment of 104 selected weapon programs using program documents, program-office questionnaires, interviews with DOD officials, and review of product-development practices; Middle Tier technology-maturity patterns are reported separately.
observations.uncertainty: The reviewed portfolio is selected by cost and acquisition status, not a random sample of all DOD programs. Delivery averages, delayed milestones, and technology maturity are program-level indicators and do not establish equal delay or failure across every system.
observations.subgroup: Major Defense Acquisition Programs and Middle Tier of Acquisition programs, including rapid prototyping and fielding pathways; program type, service, technology, and maturity differ.
observations.counterinterpretation: Entering a rapid pathway with immature technology may delay delivery, but separating immature work could also delay experimentation or reduce near-term innovation. A longer schedule can reflect testing, safety, integration, or changing requirements rather than simple administrative failure.

boundary: This record measures DOD acquisition schedules, technology maturity, and fieldable-capability status in a selected 2026 review portfolio. It does not establish operational effectiveness, deterrence, battlefield superiority, contractor causation, or the outcome of every reform.
